title: Signed closed-restriction complexes and ordered refinement chain maps
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with inverse-image coefficient rings and the actual module inverse and direct images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the canonical unit-normalized adjunctions [def-sfb-proetale-unit-normalized-adjunction]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $i_a:Z_a\hookrightarrow X$, $1\leq a\leq m$, be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], with each $i_a$ factoring through $i$. Let $M$ range over $A$-module sheaves. Assume their complementary open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] are quasi-compact morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $m\geq1$; no covering hypothesis is needed. For a nonempty subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $Z_J$ be the scheme-theoretic intersection (the iterated fibre product over $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]), and put $E_J=i_{J,*}i_J^*$ and $E_Z=i_*i^*$. For $J\subseteq L$, let $r_{J,L}:E_J\to E_L$ be the actual unit of $Z_L\hookrightarrow Z_J$ pushed to $X$, with inverse-image composition identifications; define $r_{Z,J}$ similarly. Write $D^{-1}(M)=E_Z(M)$, $D^p(M)=\bigoplus_{|J|=p+1}E_J(M)$ for $0\leq p<m$, and $D^p=0$ otherwise. Use cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The proposed differential is
$$ (dc)_{(a_0<\cdots<a_{p+1})}=\sum_{t=0}^{p+1}(-1)^t r_{L\setminus\{a_t\},L}(c_{L\setminus\{a_t\}}),\qquad d^{-1}=(r_{Z,\{a\}})_a. $$
These formulas define an augmented cochain complex, additive and natural in $M$, with
$$r_{L,H}r_{J,L}=r_{J,H},\qquad r_{Z,J}\eta_i=\eta_{i_J},\qquad d^2=0.$$
In particular its degree-zero augmentation $\alpha_M:E_Z(M)[0]\to D^{\geq0}(M)$ satisfies $\alpha_M\eta_i=(\eta_{i_a})_a$.
Let $W_b\hookrightarrow Z$, $1\leq b\leq n$, $n\geq1$, be a second ordered closed family with quasi-compact complementary open immersions in $X$. Let $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$ be any function and choose factorizations $W_b\hookrightarrow Z_{f(b)}$ over $Z$. For an increasing tuple $B=(b_0<\cdots<b_p)$ define the component of $\rho_f:D_Z^p(M)\to D_W^p(M)$ as zero if the tuple $(f(b_0),\ldots,f(b_p))$ repeats an index; otherwise use its sorting-permutation sign times the actual restriction $E_{\{f(b_0),\ldots,f(b_p)\}}(M)\to i_{W_B,*}i_{W_B}^*M$ from that summand, and zero from all other summands. Set its degree $-1$ component to the identity of $E_Z(M)$.
Then $\rho_f$ is a chain map, $\rho_f\alpha_Z=\alpha_W$, identity refinements give identity maps, and maps for iterated refinements compose. The construction, differential, and refinement maps commute with morphisms of $M$ and with parameter diagrams, meaning application objectwise to any small category of such data. Applied termwise to a cochain complex $K$, they commute with its differential and give maps of the finite total complexes with differential $d_D+(-1)^p d_K$. No exactness of the augmented rows is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-signed-closed-row-exists] separately to every ordered closed family and assemble a collection of rows by classical choice inside this existence proof. Apply [lem-sfb-signed-closed-row-maps] to this supplied collection to obtain the mixed restrictions and natural row chain maps, with their matrix, augmentation, identity and composition equations. This is only logical assembly of existential witnesses; no definition chooses data from either unproved existence statement.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, for closed units only; signed construction is the agent deduction from the ordered alternating cochains of cohomology.tex, Tag 01FG, split from lem-sfb-closed-restriction-signed-refinements.

proof.text: For each row chain map rho, apply NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex termwise to the input complex K, then whisker by the flip functor and the total functor. This is a chain map by construction, natural in K. HomologicalComplex₂.ιTotal_map gives its component on every (p,q) diagonal inclusion. The chosen flip is exactly the existing finiteClosedDouble convention, so the component is rho_(K^q)^p, and the differential is d_D+(-1)^p d_K for arbitrary unbounded K.

proof.text: Evaluate the row augmentation equation alpha_F ≫ rho = alpha_G at M and at degree zero. Rewrite alpha_f and cancel the canonical isomorphism from the degree-zero term of the single complex. This gives augment_F(M) ≫ rho_M^0 = augment_G(M). In degree n rewrite both total augmentation formulas. The diagonal-inclusion equation for the total map at (0,n), followed by this augment equation, proves preservation of total augmentation. Natural-transformation and complex-morphism extensionality yield the required equation. Insert these maps and equations, together with all row-level fields, into SignedClosedRefinementSystem.
